leads.title: China pledges to donate USD 300,000 in humanitarian assistance to Sudan to help with flood recovery in September 2020
leads.description: In 2020, China offered to donate 300,000 USD worth of humanitarian aid to Sudan to help with flood recovery. The donation was announced at a virtual reception at the Chinese Embassy in Khartoum. The floods and torrential rains that hit Sudan killed tens of peoples and destroyed thousands of houses.
leads.staff_comments: 1. AidData codes this project as 'pledge' as there is no evidence of a financial agreement or an actual transfer of monetary assistance.

leads.title: China grants $200,000 to Laos in emergency assistance for disaster relief
leads.description: On November 7, 2009, the Chinese government issued a $200,000 grant in emergency assistance for disaster relief to Laos. In September 2009, Typhoon Ketsana hit Laos' southern provinces. 19 people were killed and property losses in the storm-hit provinces were estimated at about $100 million. The grant was used in support of recovery and reconstruction in the stricken area.

leads.title: Government of China provides USD $300,000 grant to Myanmar Ministry of Social Welfare, Relief, and Resettlement in December 2021
leads.place: The purpose of the project is to provide USD $300,000 grant to Myanmar Ministry of Social Welfare, Relief, and Resettlement in December 2021. More detailed location information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/286243025.
leads.description: On December 30, 2021, the Chinese ambassador to Myanmar Chen Hai presented a donation of USD $300,000 to Union Minister of Social Welfare, Relief, and Resettlement Dr. Thet Thet Khaing. The donation is part of a USD 1,000,000 annual donation 'for the peace process in Myanmar.'

leads.title: China Ministry of Public Security donates security materials for Madagascar Police Material Purchase Project
leads.place: The project donated security materials to the Ministry of Public Security in Antananarivo, Madagascar. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/27565116
leads.description: On February 28, 2018, the Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar, Yang Xiaorong, took part in a signing ceremony for an Exchange of Letters Agreement with the Madagascar Ministry of Security. The letters specified that China's Ministry of Security would donate a batch of crime fighting materials to the Madagascar Ministry of Public Security. This agreement is seen as a way to strengthen diplomatic ties between China and Madagascar. This project is part of a continued investment on China's part in Madagascar's domestic security forces.   On July 25, 2019, the Government Procurement Office under the Chinese Ministry of Public Security announced a tender for the production of police equipment for the Ministry of Public Security Assisted Madagascar Police Material Purchase Project (Chinese project title: 公安部援马达加斯加警用物资采购项目). On September 6, 2019, China Machine International Tendering Co. Ltd. won the bid and will be carrying out the project for RMB 1.765 million (funded by China Ministry of Public Security). The equipment was to be delivered 51 days after the contract signing.  The equipment included 100 gas masks (RMB 480 each), 100 bulletproof vests (RMB 1,350 each), 100 police batons (RMB

leads.title: China agreed to provide a batch of farm tools worth US$130,000 which the GoU distributed to the Internally Displaced Person (IDPs)
leads.description: In 2006, China agreed to provide a batch of farm tools worth US$130,000 which the GoU distributed to the Internally Displaced Person (IDPs) in Northern Uganda.

leads.title: China funds freshwater fish cultivation project
leads.place: The purpose of this project was to provide farming demonstrations and technical training for agricultural cooperatives in the ADZOPE Area. More detailed locational information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/1225847163
leads.description: On May 31, 2006 and June 8, 2006, China and Cote d'Ivoire signed letters of exchange on a freshwater fish cultivation technical assistance project. As part of the agreement, 2 experts and 1 translator will be sent to Cote d'Ivoire. The team left on January 24, 2007 for Cote d'Ivoire. It was reported that the agreement is worth 1 million RMB.  The project is to provide farming demonstrations and technical training for agricultural cooperatives in the ADZOPE region. The handover of the donated fishing equipment and machinery took place 6/20/2007.

leads.title: Chinese Government donates a batch of medical supplies worth $220,000 to fight Yersinia pestis plague (Linked to Project ID #58725, #60995, #60996)
leads.description: On October 12th, 2017, China donated a package of medical supplies worth 220,000 USD to the Malagasy Ministry for Public Health to fight the Yersinia pestis plague which, at the time, had resulted in 57 fatalities. Chinese Ambassador to Madagascar Yang Xiaorong spoke at the ceremony held in Antananarivo. The package, which includes medical equipment, antibiotics, clothing, masks, and protective gloves, was ready to use immediately. A November 2017 report by ReliefWeb noted that 220,000 USD in medicines were received by the Malagasy government._x000D_ _x000D_ The leader of the 21st Chinese medical team (project #60028) attended the ceremony. This is part of a protocol signed by the two governments to regularly dispatch Chinese medical teams to Madagascar. A few days before this ceremony, the leader of the 21st medical team also gave a public lecture on plague prevention at the Chinese Embassy in Madagascar (project #61025)._x000D_ _x000D_ This is linked to projects #58725, #60995, and #60996.

leads.title: China grants Kyrgyzstan 150,000 USD for earthquake relief
leads.description: On Oct.13, 2008, Chinese government gave US$150 thousand in assistance to victims of the earthquake (happened in Oct.5) in the south of Kyrgyzstan, according to press service of the Chinese Embassy in Bishkek. "We sincerely share pain and grief of family members of those who died in the quake and wish the soonest recovery to the injured," said in the message of the Chinese Embassy.

leads.title: China donates US$100 000 in emergency aid to Vietnam for bird flu (link to project ID:#34482)
leads.description: On 10 February 2004, China donated US$100, 000 to Vietnam in order to combat the bird flu virus. No details were given regarding how the grant would be used. _x000D_ _x000D_ Over 2,500 communes in 57 cities and provinces in Vietnam have been struck by the H5N1 strain of avian influenza, which killed and led to the culling of over 38.1 million birds, 15 percent of the country's poultry. _x000D_ _x000D_ _x000D_

leads.title: China grants IOM US$200,000 to provide emergency humanitarian aid for Syrian refugees in Jordan and Lebanon
leads.description: On January 30, 2013 the Government of China granted the International Organization for Migration (IOM) US$200,000 to provide emergency humanitarian aid to Syrian refugees in Jordan and Lebanon. he aid was intended to respond to civil unrest in Syria and contributed to the IOM's 2013 Regional Refugee Response Plan (RRP) for Jordan (UN project code SRRP-13/MS/58134/R). 3RP requested USD$2.98bn for the implementation of its plan, but only USD$2.18bn was raised by member states in 2016. The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (UNOCHA) reported that China's contribution has been paid. This project is captured by UNOCHA flow #101987.

leads.title: Chinese Government provides $200,000 grant for FSM-China Friendship Sports Center Renovation Project (Linked to Project ID#40010, #64113)
leads.place: The purpose of this project was to renovate the FSM-China Friendship Sports Center on the Pohnpei campus of the College of Micronesia (COM) in advance of the 8th Micronesian Games. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/316743697.
leads.description: In August 2010, China’s Vice Foreign Minister "confirmed China's willingness to provide additional assistance" to upgrade upgrading the country's sports facilities in preparation for the 8th Micronesian Games in 2014. China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) subsequently provided a grant to the Government of the Federated States of Micronesia to renovate the FSM-China Friendship Sports Center on the Pohnpei campus of the College of Micronesia (COM) in advance of the 8th Micronesian Games. The renovation involved the refurbishing of a court and the installation of a new electronic scoreboard, lights, sound system, and NBA-style backboards and shot clocks. The renovated Sports Center was officially re-opened on February 24, 2017.
leads.staff_comments: This project is also known as the Pohnpei Multipurpose Gymnasium Upgrade Project or the College of Micronesia Stadium Renovation Project. The Chinese project title is 中密友好体育馆改造升级 or 密中友谊运动中心项目.The Chinese Government originally financed the construction this facility between 1999 and 2002 for about $5 million (as captured via Project ID#40010) and repairs to the scoreboard in 2006 (as captured via Project ID#64113).

leads.title: China grants $200,000 USD for humanitarian aid for displaced South Sudanese (linked with #41617)
leads.description: On January 23, 2014, the Chinese government granted a cash donation of US$200,000 for humanitarian aid to people displaced by the recent conflict in South Sudan._x000D_ _x000D_ On the same day, the Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan announced that China would provide USD 3 million worth of material assistance to South Sudan (project #41617).

leads.title: China donates agricultural materials to China-Samoa demonstration farm
leads.description: On April 11, 2011, China donated a batch of agricultural materials to the China-Samoa Agricultural Technology Cooperation Demonstration Farm. The donation was made by Jia Qinglin, the chairman of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC), and is worth 1 million RMB. On May 19, 2011, the Chinese Ambassador to Samoa visited the farm for their Open Day, with nearly 2000 people attending. _x000D_ _x000D_ The demonstration farm was originally built in June 2010 (see project #49231).

leads.title: Chinese Government provides RMB 1 million grant for Agricultural Technology Demonstration Center Project in Abuja (Linked to Project ID#52506)
leads.place: This project is located in the CGCOC Abuja high-tech agricultural industrial park, which is in Bwari District and Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja. More detailed locational information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/11177511134
leads.description: On 4 July, 2016, the Chinese Government and the Government of Nigeria signed an RMB 1 million grant agreement for an Agricultural Technology Demonstration Center (ATDC) Project. The funding for this project will be drawn from the proceeds of a grant that the Chinese Government previously committed through an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) in 2012 (see umbrella Project ID#52506). The purpose of this project is to establish an agricultural demonstration center in the CGCOC Abuja high-tech agricultural industrial park (阿布贾农业高科技产业园区). It will involve housing construction, access roads, water conservancy projects, and ancillary facilities.   The housing construction is about 3,500 square meters, and the other projects are about 20,000 square meters. The contract period is 15 months. It is envisaged that the ATDC will conduct agricultural cooperation and development research, full-course agricultural mechanization operation technology demonstration, water-saving irrigation technology, small-scale agricultural product processing technology, and water and soil resource utilization demonstration. China Railway 14th Bureau is the contractor responsible for project implem
leads.staff_comments: The Chinese project title is 援尼农业示范中心项目 or 尼日利亚农业示范中心项目. This project should not be confused with the agricultural demonstration area in Sokoto State (captured in Project ID#61810).

leads.title: China donates 4 million Baht to fire victims in Thailand
leads.place: China donates 4 million Baht to fire victims from the Zantika Pub fire in the Watthana District of Bangkok, Thailand. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/2938036.
leads.description: In September 2009, the Ministry of the Public Health (MOPH) distributed 4 million Baht in donations from the Chinese government to 18 seriously injured victims of the Zantika Pub fire. Deputy Public Health Minister, Manit Nop-amornbodi, and the Chinese Ambassador to Thailand, Guan Mu, presided over the presentation ceremony._x000D_

The finances go through the World Health Organization (WHO) and are to be used for the Syrian Refugee and Resilience plan. The Chinese monetary contribution was distributed but the project implementation status is unknown.

leads.title: Chinese Government provides RMB 1 million grant to PowerChina Kunming Engineering Corporation for resettling refugees in Kachin State, Myanmar (Linked to Project ID #90818)
leads.place: The purpose of the project is to support feasibility study for resettling refugees in Kachin State, Myanmar  More detailed locational information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/5996476

The purpose of this project is to house IDPs.   2) In July 2020, RMB 1 million was given to PowerChina Kunming Engineering Corporation to conduct a feasibility study for resettling refugees (see Project ID #93313). Further implementation details are unknown.  It is unclear how the remaining RMB 195 million was spent.

leads.title: Chinese company donates $100,000 to Myanmar for cyclone relief (linked to #35871 and #35872)

leads.title: Embassy of China in Myanmar donates 200 million kyats to support the cash for work program
leads.place: This project involves financing for resettlement efforts in Rakhine, Myanmar. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/5996483.

leads.title: Chinese Government provides EUR 112,700 grant for renovation and reconstruction of gyms and sports fields at four Montenegrin schools
leads.place: This project supported the renovation and reconstruction of gyms and sports fields at Ristan Pavlović Elementary School in the city of Pljevlja, Kotor Secondary Maritime School in the city of Kotor, and the Petar Lubarda High School of Fine Arts in the city of Cetinje. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/210292091#map=14/42.3954/18.9140 and https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/2353798884 and https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/236424630
leads.description: On June 22, 2017, the Chinese and Montenegrin governments signed a donation agreement in which China agreed to provide €112,700 EUR of non-refundable money for the renovation and reconstruction of gyms and school sports fields of two primary and two secondary schools in Montenegro. Elementary School "Ristan Pavlović" in Pljevlja, was to receive €23,194.38 EUR for the renovation of its gym, which was to include the replacement of the existing dilapidated parquet and the substructure. €11,987.22 EUR was allocated for the rehabilitation of the Cetinje Gymnasium, used by the students of High School of Fine Arts "Petar Lubarda."   The project included a renovation of the parquet, a paint job for the hall and locker rooms, and a solution to the gym's lighting and heating problems. The largest section of the project, the Gymnasium of the Kotor Secondary Maritime School (also known as the Kotor Maritime Middle School), was to receive €55,535.57 EUR, and included the procurement of materials, the removal of concrete, the installation of an elastic sports floor and rubber base on the stands, and the reconstruction of walls, roof and locker rooms. €21,982.83 EUR was allocated for the renovati
leads.staff_comments: One Chinese project title is 中小学体育馆项目都. Another, more specific Chinese project title for the Kotor Secondary Maritime School's gymnasium is 中黑合作科托尔海事中学体育馆修复项. Still another Chinese project title is 校园体育巩固项目.

leads.title: Embassy of China in Myanmar provides 160 million kyats worth of commodities to displaced persons in Myanmar's northern state (linked to project #86477)
leads.place: This project involves the donation of necessities to residents of Kachin State, Myanmar. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/5996476.
leads.description: On November 20, 2018, the Embassy of China in Myanmar provided rice, cooking oil, blankets, and other daily necessities worth 160 million kyats to the displaced people in the surrounding areas of Myitkyina in Kachin State, along with a donation of 12 million kyats worth of medicine (recorded in the linked project #86477). leads.title: Chinese Consulate donates USD$105,275 for Hurricane Relief
leads.place: The transitional facility is located in Sucker Garden, Dutch Sint Maarten. More specific locational information was unavailiable. See more here: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/524337653
leads.description: During the week of November 1st 2017, the Chinese Consulate in Willemstad donated a check worth USD$105,275 to the Government of Sint Maarten. The donation served as budgetary support for the reconstruction of Schools and Homes after the devastation caused by hurricane Irma. The donation was handed over by the Vice Consul and received by Prime Minister William Marlin. As of 16 August 2018 the money was utilized with the Consulate-General’s approval for start-up and monthly costs associated with the Hurricane Irma Reintegration Program Shelter, which is located in Sucker Garden. The Hurricane Irma Reintegration Program Shelter (HIRPS) aims to help homeless people reintegrate themselves back into society after being displaced as a result of the devastation suffered by Hurricane Irma in 2017. There are Three Social Workers active at the shelter, whose tasks include; counseling, assisting with resumes and job coaching, assisting with find apartments for rent, assisting the seniors in addition to several other tasks. According to local media, the shelter was scheduled to close in January 2020, however the program has been extended twice since then, and continues to operate as of June 20
leads.staff_comments: Sint Maarten is not ODA-eligible

More detailed locational information can be found at: Mandoul: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/3218250Salamat: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/3106489BET: https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/322128217
leads.description: On January 13, 2020, Chad’s Ministry of the Environment and the Chinese Embassy in Chad signed a CFA 43 billion grant agreement for a Water Supply Project. The agreement was signed by Chad’s Minister of the Environment, Brahim Mahamat Djamaladine, and the Chinese Ambassador to Chad, Li Jin Jin. The project involves the provision and installation of 510 human-powered pumps, 57 drinking water supply points, 18 pastoral wells and 129 sanitation works in three Chadian provinces: Mandoul, Salamat and BET. leads.title: Chinese Embassy donates UGX 194,444,444 to Office of the Prime Minister for flood victim relief
leads.place: The project was to provide relief supplies to families affected by disasters, particularly earmarked for those in Kasese, Bundibugyo, and Kween districts. More detailed locational information can be found at: Kasese: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/3501895Bundibugyo: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/3501892Kween: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/3501838
leads.description: On July 14, 2020, the Chinese Embassy donated 194,444,444 Uganda Shillings (~USD 50,000) to Uganda's Office of the Prime Minister as emergency humanitarian assistance for people impacted by floods in a number of communities across Uganda. Over 300,000 Ugandas were displaced and lost livelihood due to natural disasters, including these floods, locusts, and COVID-19. The Chinese Ambassador to Uganda, Zheng Zhuqiang, delivered the donation to three members of the Ugandan Cabinet: Hillary Onek, Grace Kwiyucwiny, and Musa Ecweru.  In western Uganda districts of Kasese, Bundibugyo and Ntoroko, over 110,000 people were displaced by floods in May 2020 that razed hundreds of acres of food crops to the ground. The ambassador stated that the donation was also reciprocation of support provided by Uganda to China in the early days of the COVID-19 pandemic. Ecweru thanked China for the donation and said the funding would be used to provide relief supplies to families affected by disasters in Kasese, Bundibugyo and Kween.
leads.staff_comments: 1. The picture of the check in SourceID#166842 details the funding and receiving organizations, as well as the exact transaction amount and currency.

leads.description: On July 9, 2014, the Chinese Ambassador to Pakistan, Sun Weidong, presented a donation of 5 million Pakistani Rupees to a Pakistani official on behalf of the Chinese embassy for the resettlement of internal displaced persons in Pakistan. The check was accepted by Abdul Qadir Baloch, minister of Pakistan's Ministry of States and Frontier Regions (SAFRON) for the resettlement of the internally displaced persons (IDPs) from North Waziristan_x000D_ _x000D_ The surge in internally displaced population was caused by Operation Zarb-e-Azb, a military campaign launched by the Pakistani armed forces on June 15 against domestic local militant groups hiding in North Waziristan tribal regions. SAFRON officials reported that more than 833,000 people have been registered as IDPs as a result of the operation.

leads.title: Chinese Government donates $20,000 USD in cash to Vietnam following the September 2000 Mekong Delta Floods

leads.title: China provides $100,000 Tala for Phase 5 of China-Samoa Agricultural Technical Aid Project (Linked to Project ID #61282, 49231, 49190, 61281)
leads.place: The office of the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries Samoa is located in Apia, Samoa. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/191008704.
leads.description: In 2021, China provided $100,000 Tala toward Phase 5 of the China-Samoa Agricultural Technical Aid Project. The project includes a demonstration farm that exhibits new farming techniques to increase crop yield and decrease pest effects. Past phases of the project have been running since 2010. The media first reported that the project "will move to Phase 5" on May 3, 2021.  Phase 5 has focused specifically on improving sector coordination and investment in food security, as well as creating more inclusive agricultural production systems. Over the course of the project, more than 10,000 Samoans have been trained in modern farming techniques, significantly increasing the country's ability to produce fruits and vegetables.
leads.staff_comments: 1. The Commitment/Start dates are both estimates from the source 169013, which first reported Phase 5.

leads.title: Chinese Embassy Donates 20 Mobile Toilets worth 460,000 NAD to Namibia
leads.place: The purpose of this project was to donate 20 Mobile Toilets in Khomas Province, NamibiaMore detailed location information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/2279585
leads.description: On December 13, 2018, China officially donated 20 mobile toilets worth 460,000 NAD to Khomas Province in Namibia. leads.title: China provides additional funding for the piggery at the agricultural demonstration farm (linked to projects #39252, #39248, #39241, #65028, #65029) [Subproject of #37704]
leads.place: The purpose of the project is to provide additional funding for the piggery at the agricultural demonstration farm. More detailed location information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/4611952#map=13/-21.1987/-175.2172
leads.description: On January 1st, 2009, China agreed to provide 3 million pa'anga to Tonga for development needs. Of this 3 million, 50,000 was utilized as funding for the agricultural demonstration farm project phase 1 (see #39248). It was utilized for building a new piggery with a capacity of 100 pigs and collecting waste to use for fuel and fertilizer. China provided experts to implement the project as well as equipment. The Ha'apai high school renovations and phase 1 of the agricultural demonstration farm are linked, with both implemented on April 22 2008. The farm was operational and handed over to Tonga by December 15th 2010. The technical experts are recorded in project #39252. This project is a subproject of #37704, which records the full 3 million pa'anga. This project is also linked to phases 2, 3 and 4 of the agricultural demonstration farm, recorded in #39241, #65028 and #65029 respectively.

leads.title: Monetary donation for internally displaced persons
leads.description: On Thursday, May 15, 2008, the Kenyan President gave a speech thanking the Chinese government for their monetary donation to benefit internally displaced persons. The Chinese embassy gave $23,000 US dollars to the fund for resettlement from the post-election crisis.

leads.title: China AVIC International donates $30,000 worth of thermal scanner to Zambia to prevent ebola (linked with project ID #40924)
leads.place: Lusaka
leads.description: On September 18, 2014, Health Minister Joseph Kasonde declared the launch of the US$30,000 worth Thermal Scanner donated by AVIC International at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport in Lusaka. The minister said Zambia had no reason not to succeed in the fight against Ebola as the country had put the necessary preventive measures in place. Dr Kasonde said Zambia was benefiting from China in strengthening the health system against the deadly virus, among other conditions. Chinese Ambassador to Zambia Yang Youming said the donation was worth celebrating as the Thermal Scanner would come in handy in the fight against Ebola and that AVIC International's gesture was a demonstration of the friendship from the Chinese community in Zambia. AVIC International civilian representative Xu Fei said the Kenneth Kaunda International Airport donation had brought the total Thermal Scanners donation cost to $60,000 following a similar donation at Simon Mwansa Kapwepwe International Airport in Ndola.  This project is linked to #40924.

leads.title: CNPC donates ₸10 million KZT to the Kazakh National Academy of Choreography for the purchase of medical equipment (Linked to Project ID#73476 and #88564)
leads.place: The Kazakh National Academy of Choreography was located in Astana (now Nur-Sultan). More detailed locational information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/499328449#map=17/51.09922/71.41962 and https://balletacademy.edu.kz/en/home-en/.
leads.description: On June 21, 2018, China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) donated ₸10 million KZT ($27,117 USD) to the Kazakh National Academy of Choreography to finance the academy's purchase of medical equipment. Specific equipment included pilates mats for stretching, massage baths for fatigue relief, and prophylactic equipment, all to improve student health and lower the risk of injury.  CNPC had previously provided $95.08 million USD for the construction of the academy, as captured by linked project ID#73476. It also donated a minibus before the Astana Expo in 2017, as capture by linked project ID#88564.

leads.title: China General Administration of Sports donates 254,000 rufiyaa worth of sports equipment to Athletics Association of Maldives
leads.description: In April 2008 the Chinese government donated athletics equipment worth 254,000 Maldivian rufiyaa to the government of the Maldives. The equipment was donated to the Athletics Association of Maldives from the China General Administration of Sports. Equipment included discus, relay batons, javelins, shot, high jump bed, high jump posts, medicine balls, starting guns, weight jackets, stopwatches and wheel measuring tapes.

leads.title: China government provides about 30 million kyats in humanitarian assistance to Myanmar's Flood Victims (linked to #86006)
leads.description: On 24 August 2016, China provided about 40 million kyats humanitarian assistance to Myanmar's flood victims, with 30 million kyats coming from the Chinese government.  This aid was sent through the Myanmar ministry of social welfare, relief and resettlement. This aid was provided by the Chinese Embassy, State Power Investment Corporation and Huawei Myanmar. This project is linked to #86006.
leads.staff_comments: During Huawei officials' meeting with Myanmar’s H.E.Vice President, they discussed the company’s activities and role in Myanmar. CEO Zhang Liman said Huawei Myanmar contributed K10 million in the donation, K40 million (US$33,000), of the Chinese embassy in Myanmar to flood victims at the Ministry of Social Welfare, Relief and Resettlement. So deduct K 10 million from the total amount as corporate aid.

leads.title: China donates 10 tons of rice and 5 tons of sugar to Mali for disaster relief
leads.description: On October 9th, 2007, China donated 10 tons of rice and 5 tons of sugar to Mali in response to flood disasters that occurred from July to September of that year.  The acceptance ceremony was at the Ministry of Internal Security and Civil Defense of Mali and was attended by Chinese Ambassador Zhang Guoqing and Malian Minister Sadio Kasama.  causing disasters in many towns and villages. The flood disaster killed nearly 10 people, injured 10 and caused 41,500 people to become homeless._x000D_ _x000D_ The sugar was worth 10,000 USD, but the total transaction cost is not known.

leads.title: Sinohydro Engineering Bureau 7 donates 50,000 Sudanese pounds to help flood refugees (linked to #30789)
leads.description: On August 21, 2013, POWERCHINA's subsidiary -- Sinohydro Engineering Bureau 7 -- donated 50,000 Sudanese pounds ($11,355) to flood refugees in Sudan. The donation ceremony was organized by the Chinese Embassy and Economic Counselor's Office where they, too, made a donation to Sudanese flood victims (see linked ProjectID#30789). Many Chinese enterprises in Sudan actively participated in the event.  Some regions and states in Sudan suffered severe flooding during the rainy season in 2013, and the persistent heavy rains caused large scale damage on buildings and infrastructure, such as roads. Hundreds were injured or killed.

leads.title: Embassy of China in Myanmar provides 12 million kyats worth of medicine to displaced persons in Myanmar (linked to project #66759)
leads.place: This project involves the donation of medicine to displaced persons in Sumprabum, Putao, and Machanbaw Townships as well as Myitkyina District. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/5996836 (Sumprabum Township), https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/5996806 (Putao Township), https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/5996695 (Machanbaw Township) and https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/5996538 (Myitkyina District).
leads.description: In November 2018, the Embassy of China in Myanmar donated 12 million kyats (USD $7,594) worth of medicine to the displaced persons in Sumprabum, Putao, Machanbaw townships and places in Myitkyina, along with a donation of 160 million kyats worth of commodities (recorded in the linked project #66759).  Chinese Ambassador to Myanmar Hong Liang pledged to continue support in the development of social welfare, economy, education and health for the people in Kachin State.

leads.title: Bank of China provides a IDR 100 million grant to Lombok, Indonesia for earthquake efforts
leads.place: This donation supported Lombok, Indonesia.
leads.description: On August 24, 2018, the Jakarta Branch of the Bank of China donated IDR 100 million to Lombok, Indonesia. The purpose of the donation was to support recovery efforts in the wake of a destructive earthquake. On August 19, 2018, six earthquakes occurred in the West Nusa Tenggara Province of Lombok. Five aftershocks followed on August 20, 2018. The natural disaster killed over 500 people and injured over 7,000. NU CARE-LAZISNU was the formal recipient of the grant and was responsible for organizing provisions with the donation money.  The funds were to be used to issue several emergency response kits, including those containing food (rice, instant noodles, eggs, cooking oil, sugar, biscuits, milk), emergency response materials (emergency school kits, trauma care items), health services equipment (sanitation kits, sanitation equipment, counseling services), refugee response items (household kits, tarps, tents, quilts, mats, baby diapers, elderly diapers, telon oil), and infrastructure recovery (portable toilets, bathing toilets, places of worship).

leads.title: Chengdu, China, provides masks to Zapopan City, Mexico in July 2020
leads.place: The city of Chengdu provided masks to the General Hospital of Zapopan in Zapopan City, Mexico.  More detailed locational information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/4354914191
leads.description: On July 2, 2020, the city of Chengdu, a province of Sichuan in China, donated 20,000 masks to Zapopan, its Mexican sister city. The masks are three-layered and have received guaranteed protection for contamination and medical use requirements.   The masks will be distributed to staff at the General Hospital of Zapopan for the reinforcement of health protection measures. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.
leads.staff_comments: AidData has estimated the transaction amount for this donation based on price catalogues from the World Health Organization (WHO). Please see the TUFF Methodology for additional details.

leads.title: 20th Chinese Medical Team to Cameroon donates anti-epidemic equipment to Yaoundé Women and Children's Hospital in July 2020 (Linked to Project ID#88092)
leads.place: This project involved donating anti-epidemic materials to the Yaoundé Women and Children's Hospital. For more detailed locational information, see: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/2595993#map=19/3.90779/11.53930.
leads.description: On July 13, 2020, the 20th Chinese medical team to Cameroon provided a donation of anti-epidemic and protective materials to the Yaoundé Women and Children's Hospital. The materials included 2,400 masks, 960 hats, 90 sets of PPE, and 30 barrels of Lierkang 2% enhanced glutaraldehyde disinfectant. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. The Director of the Women’s and Children’s Hospital in Yaoundé attended the ceremony and thanked the medical team for their donation. Fang Ning, the leader of the medical team, also attended the ceremony, shared their anti-epidemic experience, and gave a demonstration of three-level protection following the material handover.   This project is linked to Project ID#88092 which describes the 20th Chinese Medical Team visit to Cameroon. This medical team arrived in 2019 and assisted Cameroon with the COVID-19 epidemic. The Yaoundé Women and Children's Hospital has also previously received Chinese aid (see Projects ID#22850, ID#58695, and ID#58632).

leads.title: China Merchants Foundation contributes to a donation of three wheelchairs worth $9,000 USD to wheelchair tennis players (Linked to Project ID#95355)
leads.description: In late June 2020, China Merchants Foundation (CMF), a foundation established by the China Merchants Group (CMG) for philanthropic endeavors, and Colombo International Container Terminals (CICT) — a joint venture between China Merchants Port (CMPort) Holdings Company Limited and Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA) — collaborated donate three custom-made, professional grade, titanium wheelchairs worth $9,000 USD (£7,200 GBP; €8,000 EUR) to three internationally-ranked Sri Lankan wheelchair tennis players, as part of CMF and CICT's support for the Wheelchair Tennis Programme of the Sri Lanka Tennis Association (SLTA). The three players were all veterans of Sri Lanka Army that became para-athletes after injuries sustained during the Sri Lankan Civil War.  CMF's contribution to the donation is captured in Project ID#95354. CICT's contribution to the donation is captured in Project ID#95355.
leads.staff_comments: 1. The specific breakdown of CMF and CICT to this $9,000 USD donation is unknown. For now, AidData has assumed that each donor contributed approximately $4,500 USD to the donation.

leads.title: China’s technical assistance project team provides living supplies to Equatorial Guinea’s Ministry of Agriculture for victims of the Bata explosion in March 2021
leads.place: China’s technical assistance project team provides living supplies to Equatorial Guinea’s Ministry of Agriculture for victims of the Bata explosion.  More detailed locational information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/12719581
leads.description: On March 10, 2021, the China-aided Equatorial Guinea Demonstration Farm Technical Assistance Project Team donated living supplies to Equatorial Guinea’s Ministry of Agriculture. The donation includes 2,000 catties of rice (2,645 pounds) and 1,000 catties of vegetables (1,322 pounds). This donation was made to support the relocation of Bata explosion victims. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. Xu Zhuangsheng, the Consul General of China in Bata, and the Minister of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry, Forestry and Environment of Equatorial Guinea attended the donation ceremony.

leads.title: CDB reschedules $290 million buyer's credit for Omo Kuraz 2 Sugar Factory Construction Project (Linked to Project ID#58656)
leads.place: The purpose of the project was to construct the Omo Kuraz 2 Sugar Factory in South Omo within South Nations Nationalities and Peoples Regional State (SNNPRS). The precise locational coordinates of the factory are 5.90692, 36.03851. More detailed locational information could be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/7981481087#map=19/5.90692/36.03851.
leads.description: On October 1, 2013, China Development Bank and Ethiopian Sugar Corporation (ESC) — an Ethiopian state-owned enterprise — signed a $290 million (ETB 5,482,041.588) buyer's credit (loan) agreement for the Omo Kuraz 2 Sugar Factory Construction Project (captured via Project ID#58656). The borrowing terms of the loan were as follows: an interest rate of 6-month LIBOR plus a 2.6% margin, a grace period of 3 years, and a maturity of 13 years. The Government of Ethiopia issued a sovereign guarantee in support of the loan. Sinosure provided buyer’s credit insurance. The borrower was expected to use the proceeds of the loan to partially finance a $682 million commercial (EPC) contract that it had signed in March 2013 with China National Complete Plant Import Export Corporation (COMPLANT) for the construction of the Omo Kuraz 2 sugar factory and Omo Kuraz 3 sugar factory.   According to the Government of Ethiopia’s Aid Management Platform (AMP), the $290 million (ETB 5,482,041.588) loan for the Omo Kuraz 2 Sugar Factory Construction Project achieved a 120% disbursement rate, with China Development Bank making 19 loan disbursements (worth ETB 6,554,551.271) between 2014 and 2018: an ETB 1,145
leads.staff_comments: 1. This project is also known as the Omo Kuraz 2 Facility Project. The Chinese project title is OMO2糖厂 or 埃塞奥姆2糖厂 or 埃塞OMO2糖厂项目 or 埃塞俄比亚OMO2糖厂项目. The Amaric project title is ኦሞ ኩራዝ 2 ስኴር ፋብሪካ. 2. The all-in interest rate (2.961%) was estimated by adding a 2.6% margin to average 6-Month LIBOR in October 2013 (0.361%). 3. leads.title: Chinese Embassy donated Covid-19 and other supplies with UNCHR to the Liberia Refugee Repatriation and Resettlement Commission in 2021
leads.place: No locational information available at this time.
leads.description: On November 2, 2021, Chinese Ambassador to Liberia H.E. Ren Yisheng attended the handover ceremony of humanitarian Covid-19 supplies for refugees in Liberia. China worked with United Nations Refugee Agency (UNCHR) to donate this batch of supplies to the Liberia Refugee Repatriation and Resettlement Commission.   The donation includes 800 cartons of instant noodles, 500 pieces of surgical face masks, 100 soccer balls, 100 radios, 100 medium-sized white boards, 100 small-sized white boards, and 100 essential balms.

leads.title: China's Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and Academy of Tropical Agricultural Sciences (CATAS) provide Tropical Crop Cultivation training for Myanmar trainees
leads.place: The training course was held online.
leads.description: On November 16, 2021, an opening ceremony marked the commencement of the 21-day online Training Course on Improved Varieties Breeding of Tropical Crops for Myanmar. The course was hosted by China's Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and delivered by the Chinese Academy of Tropical Agricultural Sciences (CATAS) and was intended to train individuals to become professionals in the field of Myanmar's tropical agriculture development. This training course arranges training courses on fine varieties of tropical crops such as flowers, sugarcane, vanilla, cassava, cocoa, rubber, lychee, coffee, etc., as well as the quality and safety of tropical agricultural products in China and the planning of modern agricultural industrial parks. Students travel to various tropical crop demonstration bases. This training course will help Myanmar cultivate more urgently needed professionals in the field of tropical agriculture, promote the development of tropical agriculture in Myanmar, expand bilateral agricultural cooperation, and benefit the Myanmar people. A total of 22 trainees participated in the course.  The course was held online because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

leads.title: Chinese Government provides relief materials to Surigao del Norte, Philippines, after destructive typhoon in December 2021
leads.place: The purpose of the project is to provide relief materials to Surigao del Norte, Philippines, after the destructive typhoon in December 2021. More detailed location information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/1507031.
leads.description: On December 28, 2021, the Chinese Government provided disaster relief materials to Surigao del Norte, a municipality in the Philippines. The materials included 3,500 food packages, bottled water, and rice. The monetary value of this donation is unknown. This donation was made as part of the Chinese Government’s overall commitment to aid the Philippines as they recover from “Rey,” a major typhoon that hit the country on December 16, 2021. As of December 28, 2021, the typhoon resulted in 389 deaths and left 570,000 people without homes.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. During the ceremony, Li Lin, the Chinese Consul General, delivered the relief materials on behalf of the Chinese Government. The Governor of Surigao del Norte, Rano Matugas, the Deputy Governor, Eddie Gaturangi, and the Mayor of Surigao City, Ernesto Matugas, also attended the handover ceremony.

leads.title: China provides grant for Phase 5 of the China-Samoa Agricultural Demonstration Farm Project (Linked to Project ID#49231, #49190, #61281, and #61282)
leads.place: The Independent State of Samoa
leads.description: On February 18, 2021, Chinese Ambassador to the Independent State of Samoa announced plans to build new agricultural infrastructure and 50 new demonstration farms in Samoa. More specific information was expressed by Li Zhiwen who is the head of the China-Samoa Agricultural Technical Aid group. He provided construction plans and details related to China's interest in pursuing the project. This project was known as the Samoa-China Agricultural Technical Aid Project (SCATAP).   On December 8, 2022, a handover ceremony was held for this project. The SCATAP Phase Five supports 58 model farmers with 30 in vegetables, 22 citrus and 6 chicken farmers.  Each vegetable model farmer received 2 x 30 x 6 tunnel houses with irrigation system, 50 trees citrus plantation for citrus farmers and a broiler house of 90 m fence for each chicken farmer. The donation also included a small-scale feed mill to make feed for poultry, pigs, cattle and fish farms.  The effort is part of the China-Samoa Agricultural Technical Aid project and is the fifth phase of that project. See project ID#49231 for Phase I, ID#49190 for Phase II, ID#61281 for Phase III, and ID#61282 for Phase IV.

leads.title: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs of China provides the Juncao Technical Training Course at the China-aided Samoa Demonstration Farm
leads.place: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs of China coordinates the Juncao Technical Training Course at the China-aided Samoa Demonstration Farm.  The event was held at the China-aided Samoa Demonstration Farm which is located in Nu'u village.  More detailed locational information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/3327914793
leads.description: On February 25, 2021, the opening ceremony for the Chinese-funded Juncao Technical Training Course was held at the Demonstration farm aided by China. The training course received funding from the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs of China and from the China-Aid SA Agricultural Technology Cooperation Project. The event marks the start of China-backed efforts to develop agriculture capacity in Samoa via the Juncao center. Chinese Ambassador to Samoa, Chao Xiaoliang, was present at the opening ceremony.

leads.title: Chinese Embassy and Chinese Consulate General jointly provide 600 food parcels to KwaZulu-Natal (KZN) locals in August 2021
leads.place: KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/349390
leads.description: On August 11, 2021, the Chinese Embassy and the Chinese Consulate General in Durban provided 600 food parcels to locals in the KwaZulu-Natal (KZN) province of South Africa. This donation was made to alleviate the stress of citizens affected by recent riots throughout the KwaZulu-Natal province. The monetary value of the donation is unknown.  A handover ceremony was held for this donation. China’s Ambassador to South Africa, Chen Xiaodong, the Chinese Consul General in Durban, Fei Mingxing, and representatives of the KZN Provincial government attended the ceremony. leads.title: Chinese Government donates disaster relief supplies after floods to Republic of Afghanistan (Linked to Project ID#88539)
leads.description: On September 20, 2020, a handover ceremony for a batch of donated non-emergency disaster relief supplies from the Chinese Government was held in Kabul, Afghanistan. Present at the ceremony were the Chinese Ambassador to Afghanistan, Wang Yu, and Afghan State Minister for Disaster Management, Ghulam Bahauddin Jailani.   The donated supplies included 1,000 tents, 60,000 blankets and 110,000 daily necessities, according to the Chinese Embassy. The donation came after floods caused damage and displaced people in Eastern Afghanistan starting on August 25, 2020.   The donation also came after an exchange of letters was signed to provide non-emergency aid to Afghanistan. See Project ID#88539 for more details on this 2019 agreement.

leads.title: China funds the establishment of a millet research center in Burkina Faso (linked to #86708)
leads.description: On September 8, 2020, Chinese Ambassador to Burkina Faso Li Jian went to Lombira Farm, located 30 kilometers northeast of Burkina Faso's capital Ouagadougou, to inaugurate the China-Burkina Faso Joint Research Center on Millet. Ambassador Li and Burkina Faso's Minister of Agriculture and Agricultural Water Governance Salifou Ouedraogo gave speeches.   The joint research center was built by CGCOC, a Chinese state owned construction group. The Chinese Ministry of Agriculture supplies 50 sets of seed testing equipment for the seed testing laboratory of the Joint Research Center. leads.title: Chinese Embassy in Cambodia provides flood relief kits to 800 families in the Dangkor district of Cambodia
leads.place: The Dangkor district is a southwestern suburb of Cambodia's capital city of Phnom Penh. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/2259498.
leads.description: On October 20, 2020, the Chinese Embassy in Cambodia provided flood relief kits to 800 families in the Dangkor district of Cambodia. Chinese Ambassador Wang Wentian, joined by Cambodian lawmaker Hun Many, president of the Union of Youth Federations of Cambodia, and Phnom Penh governor Khuong Sreng, distributed the relief items at three different locations in the district. By this time, 25 people had been killed and 37,396 others had been forced to evacuate.

leads.title: Chinese SOEs donate oil cleanup supplies to Mauritius after oil spill (linked to #92242)
leads.place: The oil spill affected a 27km area around Blue Bay Marine Park and affected nearby beaches. For more detailed locational information, see: https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/6352890485#map=16/-20.4436/57.7076.
leads.description: On July 25, 2020, a 200,000-ton Japanese freighter Wakashio ran aground near the Blue Bay Marine Park in Mauritius while on its way from China to Brazil. On August 6, 2020, the ship suffered a serious oil spill. About 1,000 tons of heavy oil leaked and polluted the nearby sea and beaches. The Mauritian government declared a state of environmental emergency on August 7th.  In response to the disaster, 15 Chinese companies, the majority of which were state owned enterprises (SOEs), donated pollution clean up supplies such as geotextiles, safety nets,  protective clothing, large iron buckets, and drones. It is unclear which company donated which supplies, and in what quantity. The total worth of the donation was about 1.37 million rupees by August 12, 2020, and was given to the Ministry of Environmental Protection of Mauritius.   The companies that participated in this donation included China State Construction Engineering, Beijing Construction Engineering, China Road and Bridge, Huawei, Sinohydro, China Jiangsu International, Tianli Spinning, Shanxi Jinfei co., China International Water & Electrical Corp, Henan Water Conservancy Investment Group, Kuanfu Tea, Yihai Properties Group, a
leads.staff_comments: 1) Transaction amount not recorded since it is unknown how much of the donation came from state-owned companies compared to private sector companies.  The total amount provided in the description is taken from the website of the Chinese Ministry of Commerce. 2) It is unclear what supplies were donated on what date and by which company. 3) Commitment date and implementation dates are estimated based on the beginning of the oil leak (Aug. 6) and the date given by MofCom of the final total of donations (Aug. 12).

leads.title: China's Shanxi Investment Construction Engineering Group donates disaster relief materials to Mauritius (Linked to Project ID #92240)
leads.place: This project involved donating relief materials to Mauritius for an oil spill near Blue Bay Marine Park. For more detailed locational information, see: https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/6352890485#map=16/-20.4436/57.7076.
leads.description: In August of 2020, Shanxi Investment Construction Engineering Group donated disaster relief materials to Mauritius following a large oil spill that took place near Blue Bay Marine Park. The oil spill took place after the Japanese freighter Wakashio ran aground near the Blue Bay Marine Park while on its way to Brazil. This crash took place on July 25, 2020.  On August 6th, oil began to leak from the ship. As of August 19, 2020, about 1,000 tons of heavy oil had leaked and polluted the nearby sea and beaches. The Mauritian government declared a state of environmental emergency.  The supplies donated by Shanxi Investment Construction Engineering Group included 200 pairs of rubber shoes, 200 pairs of rubber gloves, 300 bottles of mineral water and other relief materials. The materials were shipped to various designated locations where the company’s project staff and locals worked to make oil separators, put sugarcane leaves and plastic bottles on geotextiles, and place them in the sea to prevent the spread of oil. The donation was part of a larger effort by Chinese state enterprises to assist in the oil spill cleanup (captured in project #92240).
leads.staff_comments: 1) Commitment date is estimated based on the beginning of the oil leak (Aug. 6).

There are 22 members in the group, including eight local technicians from the Institute of Agricultural Sciences, eight technical extension staff, and six farmers. Each multi-party technician in the exchange group is responsible for 5-10 farmers. As of July 29th, 2020, the project team tested and demonstrated hybrid rice planting in the Kara area, and the yield increased by as much as 60%. The successful experiment and demonstration of dry season rice planting by Chinese experts has led to the Togolese government successively introducing a series of measures to develop agriculture, intending to promote the results of the project on a larger scale. leads.title: China donates 2554 tonnes of rice for Rohingyas living in Bangladesh
leads.place: This project was to donate 2554 tonnes of rice to Bangladesh to assist Rohingyas. The majority of Rohingyas in Bangladesh are located in the Cox's Bazar (Bengali: কক্সবাজার) region. More detailed locational information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/3824578#map=8/21.187/91.780.
leads.description: On July 5, 2019, Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina visited Beijing and signed a number of agreements with China. After meeting Chinese Premier Li Keqiang, she signed a Letter of Exchange for rice aid which is meant to assist Rohingyas displaced by the crisis in Myanmar. The project's name is "China Emergency Rice Aid Project for Rohingyas". This was one of nine agreements signed between the two countries, including an aid package for the Bangladesh-China-India-Myanmar Economic Corridor. During the same visit, Bangladesh received a US$31 billion funding package for the Bangladesh-China-India-Myanmar corridor project.   Under the agreement, China would send 2554 tonnes of rice to Bangladesh. On November 8, 2019, China shipped 200 tonnes of rice (the first batch) from Shanghai, which arrived at Chittagong Port in Bangladesh in December 2019. In July 2020, over 1300 tons arrived. On January 22, 2021, the Bangladeshi authorities announced all 2554 tons of rice have arrived. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

leads.title: Chinese Center for Disease Control aids Pakera Regional Hospital with histoplasmosis outbreak
leads.place: The project donated to Pakera Regional Hospital in the village of Matthew's Ridge and Georgetown Public Hospital. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/674938303, https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/11213168
leads.description: In April 2019, the Chinese Center for Disease Control (CCDC) committed assistance to the Pakera Regional Hospital and Georgetown Public Hospital to address a Histoplasmosis outbreak in manganese mines in Guyana, with some Chinese workers contracting the illness.  On April 6, 2019 a team of medical experts from the CCDC was compiled and deployed to Georgetown Public Hospital.  The CCDC also provided specialists, a laboratory, and x-ray equipment. From April 8 to April 10 a group of nine specialists came to aid in testing. This announcement came after an April outbreak of histoplasmosis at the Matthew's Ridge Tunnel mine that killed 2 Chinese workers and sickened 27 others.

leads.title: Yunnan Provinical Government supports the Laos Cross-border Asian Elephant Protection Area in Poor Ethnic Minority Village Ecological Demonstration Village Pilot Project.
leads.place: Baka Lao Village, Bennu County, and Phongsali ProvinceMore detailed location information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/132724948Location information for Baka Lao and Bennu county could not be found
leads.description: On May 8, 2019, the Laos Cross-border Asian Elephant Protection Area in Poor Ethnic Minority Village Ecological Demonstration Village Pilot Project was approved by the Yunnan Provincial Government for support (or 老挝跨境亚洲象保护区域贫困少数民族村寨生态示范村试点项目). The Baka Lao Village, Bennu County, and Phongsali Province were chosen for the village. The planned investment for the project is 500,000 yuan ("中方对老挝跨境亚洲象保护区生态示范村项目选址再确认"). The actual investment is unknown.  The project started in August and was completed on November 9, 2019. It was supported by the Yunnan Provincial Government, the Yunnan Provincial Department of Commerce, and the Yunnan Provincial Department of Finance, and it was jointly implemented by the Yunnan Green Environment Development Foundation and Xishuangbanna Nature Reserve Management and Protection Bureau. The project helped the villagers build a 100- cubic-meter reservoir, install 10 solar street lights, and distribute 73 fire-saving stoves to the villagers . At the same time, it also helped the local to form a 15- member community patrol team, and trained the patrol team members on the awareness of the community residents' elephant awareness and Asian elephant patrol skills

leads.title: 18th batch of Chinese peacekeeping force is sent to Lebanon (Linked to #41114)
leads.place: The Chinese peacekeeping forces were stationed at Hanniyeh Village as a part of the United Nations Interim Forces in Lebanon near Lebanon's border with Israel.  More detailed locational information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/12979796

They completed their transition ceremony with the 17th teacher on May 27th, 2019, and served a term of one year. 200 peacekeepers were in this batch.   The group was sent due to increasing protests throughout Lebanon and was stationed mostly on the border between Lebanon and Israel. The troops' camps were located in Hanniyah Village in southern Lebanon. They were composed of two plane building platoons, two three-dimensional building platoons and one combat service support platoon equipped with more than thirty types of technical personnel to assist with engineering, construction, medical treatment, consulting, and advice. Their deployment, and the deployment of other peacekeeping forces, was suspended on June 30, 2020 by the UN Secretary-General due to COVID-19.  On August 5, 2020, nine peacekeepers of the eighteenth batch were informed that they would be deployed to Beirut, Lebanon to respond to the explosion on August 4, 2020 as part of an emergency medical team. leads.title: Chinese Government provides funding for FSM-China Friendship Demonstration Farm at the College of Micronesia in 2019 (Linked to Project ID#64028)

The farm locates in the National Campus of the College in Pohnpei State. The demonstration farm includes 432 square meters of vegetable steel shed, 100 square meters of permeable pig house, and a hydraulic biogas digester (15 cubic meters). The farm covers an area of 1500 square meters. It can be at the same time to accept 100 high school students or nearby farmers to carry out vegetable cultivation, pig captivity, and biogas applications and other theoretical teaching and on-site internship activities.   The project is one of the important missions of the 11th agricultural technical assistance project (as captured via Project ID#64028). Hunan International Engineering Co., Ltd. is the contractor responsible for project implementation. Implementation started in May 2019.

leads.title: Chinese Government donates 20 trucks to Myanmar's Committee on Repatriation and Resettlement of Displaced People
leads.place: The purpose of this project was to donate trucks to the National Reconciliation and Peace Centre (NRPC), Rakhine StateMore detailed location information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/4574913591#map=16/19.7611/96.0479
leads.description: According to the news releases from the Embassy of China in Myanmar and the Ministry of Information of Myanmar, on February 27, 2019, the Chinese government donated 20 Sinotruck Howo trucks to the Myanmar Committee on Repatriation and Resettlement of Displaced People. The trucks will help the Myanmar government to transport displaced people from Rakhine State who have returned to Myanmar as part of the resettlement and repatriation process. leads.title: Chinese Embassy Grants Humanitarian Aid to the People of Kachin in Myanmar in 2019

Speaking at the donation ceremony, Chinese Ambassador Chen Hai said that humanitarian assistance is part of the cooperation plan on China-Myanmar Economic Corridor and hoped that such assistance from China would be effective for the development of people in Kachin state. Chen also pledged continued assistance to Myanmar and further cooperation to assist Myanmar to achieve eternal peace in northern part of the country including Kachin state.  Under the humanitarian assistance program, hospital and medical equipment is donated to Kachin state's General Hospital, Heath and Treatment Department and Free Medical Treatment Foundation. Projector equipment, audio system and computers were provided to the state's Myitkyina University and commodities including rice, cooking oil and blankets to Myitkyina School for the Blinds and an orphanage named "New Hope Family Residence."

leads.title: Chinese Embassy donates 200 tents to Pakistan following Summer 2019 floods
leads.place: Dera Ismail Khan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province, Pakistan. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/279821922#map=10/31.8280/70.9085

In response, on September 15, 2019, the Chinese Embassy in Pakistan officially donated 200 tents to the Dera Ismail Khan area in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to support civilians who have been displaced by the floods. leads.title: China donates Equipment to Sindh Police
leads.place: The project provided equipment to the Central Police Office in Karachi, Sindh Province, Pakistan. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/539432944
leads.description: On October 11, 2019, officials of the Consulate General of China donated three automobiles, fifty walkie-talkie sets, fifteen printers, two computers, a photocopy machine and a set of monitoring equipment to the Sindh Police during a ceremony at the Sindh Central Police Office. Later, Inspector General of the Sindh Police, Dr. Syed Kaleem Imam, distributed the equipment among different departments. Two mobile vans were given to Foreigners Security Cell while other items were handed over to the Special Security Unit.   The donation came 11 months after two police officers from the Sindh Police were killed while defending the Chinese Consulate in Karachi from a terrorist attack in November 2018. Five months after the attack, in June 2019, the Chinese Consul General, Wang Yu, met with the Sindh Province Chief of Police and expressed willingness to assist the Sindh Police in capacity building and personnel training.

leads.title: Chinese Embassy in South Africa and China Foundation for Peace and Development plan to implement rural poverty alleviation demonstration project

The two parties aim to create a "cow raising and poverty alleviation" cooperation, and a "company + poor household" cooperative cow breeding model has been formed. The project aims to alleviate poverty among 100 households over five years. Beijing Capital Agribusiness Group will be one of the investors of the project.  As of July 5, 2019, both countries have only gone through the preliminary planning stages of the project. No formal agreements have been made. The financing of the project is unknown.

leads.title: Chinese Government provides training for 25 members of Angola's agricultural sector

A farewell ceremony was hosted on July 8, 2018. Cui Aimin, Ambassador to Angola, Pinto, Secretary of State for Agriculture in Angola, and the Director of the Human Resources Department of the Ministry of Agriculture for Angola attended. The financial value of the training is unknown.

leads.title: China Ministry of Commerce hosts training for 258 farmers at Agricultural Technology Demonstration Center in Benin

leads.title: ICBC pledges loan to CCCC for Private Use Terminal Construction Project at Porto São Luís (Linked to Project ID #62080)
leads.place: The Porto São Luís Project in Sao Marcos Bay is proposed to support the construction of a greenfield private port terminal located in the Organized Port Complex of Itaqui, in the municipality of São Luís, State of Maranhão. The Project is strategically located to increase the north region’s capacity to drain the production of Brazil’s expanding agricultural frontier (States of Mato Grosso, Goiás, Tocantins, Pará, Maranhão, and Piauí), which will facilitate the export of grains coming from the midwest of the country, and the imports of fertilizers and liquid bulks. More detailed locational information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/10189309
leads.description: On September 1, 2016, China Communications Construction Company (CCCC) signed an investment agreement and financing framework agreement with the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) and Thorell, a Brazilian firm, for the Private Use Terminal Construction Project at Porto São Luís in Brazil. In July 2017, CCCC signed an investment agreement with WPR Participações (a Brazilian firm and subsidiary of WTorre Group) for building the terminal. Then, on March 16, 2018, ICBC, represented by ICBC Brazil, signed a financing mandate letter committing to provide a loan for this project. The loan's face value and borrowing terms are unknown. However, it is known that the purpose of this loan was to cover the 70% of the over $700 million total project cost. The remaining 30% was expected to come in the form of an equity investment from CCCC (captured via Project ID #62080).  The Private Use Terminal Construction Project at Porto São Luís is intended to improve supply chain operations in the agricultural industries from mid-West Brazil (States of Mato Grosso, Goiás, Tocantins, Pará, Maranhão, and Piauí). Works involve construction of a water port with four berths and supporting storage
leads.staff_comments: The Chinese project title is 圣路易斯港项目. The Portuguese project title is Terminal de Uso Privado (TUP) Porto São Luís. This project is also known as the Port of San Luis or Port of St. Louis. There are several unknowns for this ICBC loan. It is unclear whether it is financing just Phase 1 of the project or all phases. The ICBC source suggests the total project cost is BRL 1.7 billion (equal to about $465,227,360.85 in 2018 nominal USD) but almost all of the other sources say the 'total investment' is USD 700 million. Moreover, it is possible that a special purpose vehicle called TUP Porto São Luís S.A. contracted the ICBC loan (see NDB projects page) but this issue merits further investigation.The China-Latin America Commercial Loans Tracker, which is produced by the Inter-American Dialogue, identifies the loan commitment year as 2017. AidData codes the commitment year as 2018 since an official (CCCC) source indicates that the loan agreement was signed on March 16, 2018.

leads.title: China Conducts Seventh Phase of China-Aided Dominica Agricultural Technical Cooperation Project (Linked to Project ID #56148 and #98408)
leads.place: The purpose of this project is to implement the seventh phase of Dominica agricultural technical cooperation project, including restoring greenhouses and introducing new plants and crops. Minister Grant, from the Ministry of Blue and Economy, Agriculture and National Food Security, explained that a new model farm was set to be constructed in the Wesley community during the 2020-2021 budget debate (see 'MODEL FARM TO BE CONSTRUCTED IN WESLEY'). leads.title: Chinese Ark Peace Hospital Ship Visits Grenada in 2018 (Linked to Project ID#54956)
leads.place: The purpose of this project was to provide medical care at the Seaport of St. Georges, GrenadaMore detailed location information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/178505095
leads.description: On October 2, 2018, the Ark Peace of People's Liberation Army Navy of China arrived at St. George, the capital of Grenada, for an 8-day visit. This is the second time the ship has visited Grenada and will provide free medical services to local Grenadian people for the "Harmonious Mission-2018" tour/project from October 4 to October 7. The ship also sent 11 medical teams to various local hospitals, sports centers, and prisons to provide medical services. The Peace Ark treated 7,275 people and performed medical examinations on an additional 2,764 people. They also carried out physical examinations for 49 people, admitted 17 people into hospital and performed 15 cases of surgery. The hospital ship left the St. George's Port on October 9. The Chinese medical experts also carried out the nursing technology demonstration exchange with 40 Grenadian nursing staff and demonstrated such skills as “bone marrow aspiration” and “neonatal touch”.  The first time the ship visited Grenada and provided medical services was in 2015 (captured by Project ID#54956).
leads.staff_comments: The Chinese name of the ship is '中国海军和平方舟医院船'.
