leads.title: Chinese Government reschedules the Government of Sudan’s outstanding debt obligations in 2012
leads.description: On February 18, 2012, the Chinese Government announced that it had agreed to reschedule the outstanding debt obligations of the Government of Sudan by extending loan repayment periods by 5 years.  It is not clear whether all Chinese Government loan maturities were extended by 5 years, or a specific subset of Chinese Government loans.  According to a Khartoum-based newspaper (al-Sahafa), which cited Sudan Finance Minister Ali Mahmoud, the Chinese Government agreed to the rescheduling because of Sudan’s 'loss of oil revenues.'   At the time that this debt rescheduling agreement was finalized, Sudan had experienced a major slide in its currency after losing three quarters of its oil production due to the 2011 secession of South Sudan. The currency slide, in turn, fueled inflation and protests. Oil revenues provided the main source of foreign currency used by the Government of Sudan to repay foreign currency-denominated loans.

leads.title: China grants Cameroon new medical treatment technology and training for hina-Cameroon Capsule Endoscopy New Diagnostic and Clinical Technology Demonstration and Training Center
leads.place: More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/2595993
leads.description: An MOU was signed on December 5th of 2011 between China and Cameroon for the China-Cameroon Capsule Endoscopy New Diagnostic and Clinical Technology Demonstration and Training Center at the Yaounde Women and Children Hospital in Cameroon. The center was built by the Ministry of Science and Technology of China and implemented by Chongqing Jinshan Technology (Group) Co., Ltd. The company has presented a batch of capsule endoscopic equipment and capsules to Yaounde Women and Children Hospital as well as conducted a four-day technology training for local doctors. The center and training was completed on December 10th, 2011 (Ministry of Commerce of the People's Republic of China). _x000D_

leads.title: China MIIT signs MoU for potential financial participation in Telecommunications Project in Laos
leads.description: In June 2011, at the GMS information and communications technology (ICT) Ministerial Meeting, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) of the PRC and the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications (MPT) of the Lao PDR signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on "Continuing with Demonstration Projects of Applicable Communication Technologies in Rural Areas." The projected total cost was $5 million USD, although it is unknown how much of this value is financed by China.
leads.staff_comments: Project was co-financed with the ADB. The type and amount of Chinese financing is unknown.

leads.title: China introduces Hybrid Rice Production in Liberia (Linked to Project ID#1653)
leads.place: More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/272602735#map=15/7.0091/-9.5808
leads.description: On November 16, 2011, China-assisted Central Agricultural Research Institute Agricultural Technology Demonstration Center introduced a new hybrid rice plantation in Liberia. Chinese assistance to facilitate agricultural technology demonstration center began operations in January of this year and has planted 70 acres of rice with a yield of 400 kg per mu or more. The Chinese government and agricultural experts managed the demonstration center. On the afternoon of February 9, 2012, Liberian Minister of Ministry of Agriculture, Florence A. Chenoweth was invited to visit the hybrid rice plantation in the hybrid rice demonstration field of China Liberia-aid agricultural technology demonstration center. No information about the cost of the project could be found.  The construction of the agricultural technology demonstration center is captured by Project ID#1653.

leads.title: China Establishes Solar and Biogas Pilot Projects at Malawi Universities
leads.description: In 2011, China pledged to assist Malawi in setting up solar and biogas pilot projects at universities. The Chinese will install demonstration projects to help train renewable-energy engineers. Natural Resources, Energy, and Environment Minister Grain Malunga praised the pledge and said that the projects will be able to generate a total of 90 MW and train renewable-energy engineers. The current status of these projects and their value cannot be determined.

leads.title: Chinese government signs ETCA for free economic assistance (linked to #832 and #64051)
leads.description: On October 20, 2011, the Chinese government signed three economic and technical cooperation agreements with the government of Malawi. The three agreements included assistance for a Malawi agricultural demonstration center (#832), an unknown amount of free economic assistance, and an interest-free loan (#64051). This project is for the free economic assistance. The purpose of the grant is unknown.

leads.title: Chinese government signs ETCA for interest free loan (linked to #832 and #58118)
leads.description: On October 20, 2011, the Chinese government signed three economic and technical cooperation agreements with the government of Malawi. The three agreements included assistance for a Malawi agricultural demonstration center (#832), an unknown amount of free economic assistance (#58118), and an interest-free loan. This project is for the interest-free loan. The amount and purpose of the loan is unknown._x000D_
leads.staff_comments: Since loan terms for the interest-free loan are unavailable, AidData has set maturity period to 20 years by default and grace period to 10 years by default per China's Foreign Assistance White Paper (http://www.cidca.gov.cn/2018-08/06/c_129925064_3.htm) which states that the maturity period of interest-free loans is 20 years, with a drawdown period of 5 years, grace period of 5 years, and repayment over 10 years. AidData treats the drawdown period as providing 5 years of additional grace.

leads.title: China implements phase 8 of technical cooperation for the Pohnpei Pilot Farm in Micronesia (Linked to Umbrella Project #64557)
leads.place: This project supported the Pohnpei Demonstration Farm in the town of Pohnlangas within the municipality of Madolenihmw on the island of Pohnpei. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.google.com/maps/place/Chinese+Farm+Rd,+Pohnpei,+Federated+States+of+Micronesia/@6.837091,158.2939304,19z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m5!3m4!1s0x65d9b72ce5c52fa1:0x94238234ab7dd51f!8m2!3d6.8370897!4d158.2944776 and https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/551283612.
leads.description: On November 25, 2011, the Chinese Ambassador and Micronesian Minister of Foreign Affairs signed an exchange of letters for phase 8 of a technical cooperation project on the Pohnpei pilot farm (or Pohnpei Demonstration Farm or 援密第八期佩州示范农场技术合作项目) in Micronesia. At the time of signing, phase 8 was planned to begin in 2011 and end in 2013. Umbrella project #64557 captures all 11 phases of technical cooperation._x000D_ _x000D_ According to a November 2011 ECCO articles, phase 8 was planned to begin in 2011 and end in 2013. A 2015 article from the Chinese Ministry of Commerce reports that phase 8 ended on November 25, 2013. The implementing contractor is unknown. _x000D_ _x000D_ The farm is located in the state of Pohnpei spanning 80,000 square meters including 40,000 square meters of tropical rain forests. The farm cultivates crops like sakau, yam, taro, banana, and others. The remaining 40,000 square meters houses laboratories, offices, and greenhouses. The purpose of this bilateral cooperation is to train local Micronesian farmers, introduce new seeds, and transfer agricultural technology to increase productivity. The phase 8 team provided more than 10,000 seedlings of cucumber, cabba

leads.title: [Suspended] China Development Bank contributes to loan syndicate for 6000MW Myitsone Hydropower Plant Construction Project
leads.place: The purpose of the project was to construct a 6000MW hydroelectric power plant and dam at the confluence of the Mali and N’mai rivers and the source of the Irawaddy River (Ayeyawady River). The dam site is 3.2 kilometres (2.0 mi) below the confluence of the Mali River and the N'Mai River about 42 km (26 mi) north of Myitkyina, the capital of Kachin State, in northern Burma. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/206336254.
leads.description: In December 2006, State Power Investment Corporation (SPIC) signed a memorandum of cooperation with Myanmar’s Ministry of Electric Power (MoEE) No. 1 to develop 2 hydropower plant projects, one of which was the 6000MW Myitsone Hydropower Plant Construction Project. Then, on February 20, 2010, a joint venture called the Upstream Ayeyawady Confluence Basin Hydropower (UACBH) Company was created by MoEE (15% ownership stake), SPIC (80% ownership stake), and Asia World Company (5% ownership stake) to manage the design, financing, and implementation of the 6000MW Myitsone Hydropower Plant Construction Project.   In early 2011, an RMB-denominated syndicated loan was issued (mostly likely to UACBH) for the 6000MW Myitsone Hydropower Plant Construction Project. China Development Bank (CDB) contributed to the loan, but the size of its contribution is unknown. The borrowing terms of the loan are also unknown. However, it is known that as a source of collateral (security), the Government of Myanmar pledged its shares in the the joint venture. Future revenues (electricity sales) from the power plant were expected to be use to facilitate loan repayment.    The purpose of the project was to cons
leads.staff_comments: After fifty years of operation, UACBH was to become 100% Myanmar-owned.

leads.title: China signs contract for solar energy demonstration project
leads.place: On December 22, 2011, the Chinese Ambassador to Niger, the Niamey Mayor, and City Council Speaker signed a contract for a solar energy demonstration project. For more detailed location information: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/3218804
leads.description: On December 22, 2011, the Chinese Ambassador to Niger, the Niamey Mayor, and City Council Speaker signed a contract for a solar energy demonstration project. The project will be implemented by Zhongxing Technologies and is estimated to be completed in four months. The financial amount for this project cannot be found.  On January 1, 2022, a ceremony honoring China-aided Mali Solar Energy Demonstration Village project in Koneobra village, where off-grid solar systems, solar street light systems, solar water pump systems, and some centralized solar power supply systems are directly benefiting tens of thousands of local people.

leads.title: China Donates Anti-malarial Medicine to Niger (December)
leads.description: On 21 December 2011, the Chinese Government officially donated anti-malarial drugs in pursuit of the Nigerien President's national campaign to reduce malaria-induced death rates. The value and quantity of medicine are unknown.

leads.title: China to establish an Agricultural Demonstration Center in Pakistan
leads.description: On 28 April 2011, Dr. Muhammad Afzal, Chairman of the Pakistan Agricultural Research Council (PARC), launched the idea of establishing an “Agriculture Demonstration Centre” in Pakistan for training of farmers, demonstration of technologies, and development of new hybrid crop varieties. This project was declared during a meeting with a 4 member high level delegation from China headed by Mr. Hu Yuahan, Director General of China's Foreign Cooperatives Committee for the Ministry of Agriculture at the PARC in April 2011. In addition to cooperation with China, Pakistan can learn an efficient system of agricultural research, increase agricultural production and productivity, and also facilitate access to China's vast market.

leads.title: China builds solar streetlights in Khartoum, Sudan
leads.place: The purpose of the project is to build solar streetlights in Khartoum. More detailed location information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/164057559#map=19/15.60558/32.51131
leads.description: On September 29, 2011 and February 19, 2012, China and the Sudan governments signed a letter of exchange regarding the solar energy demonstration project in Sudan (援苏太阳能示范项目). At the request of the Sudan government, the Chinese government agreed to assist in the construction of a solar street lamp project in the Friendship Hall of Khartoum, the capital of Sudan. _x000D_ _x000D_ From June 2 to June 10 in 2011, the Chinese Ministry of Commerce sent a group to conduct a feasibility study on the Solar Energy Demonstration Project, which involved building a set of solar streetlights for the Sudan Friendship Hall in Khartoum. This project is one of eight initiatives proposed during the Fourth Ministerial Conference of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation to assist African countries in small-scale clean energy projects. The value or amount of solar lights is unknown.

leads.title: China donates 26 sets of biogas equipment to Taba Village, White Nile State, Sudan
leads.place: The purpose of the project is to donate 26 sets of biogas equipment to Taba Village, White Nile State, Sudan. More detailed location information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/3774676
leads.description: On October 8, 2011, Counsellor Liu Zengxian and relevant staff of  the Chinese Embassy in Sudan traveled to Taba village in the White Nile state to donate 26 sets of biogas equipment as part of the White Nile Biogas Phase II Demonstration Project (白尼罗州沼气二期示范项目). The biogas equipment was donated and built by the Embassy. The biogas project as a successful and beneficial attempt not only improved the living conditions of local villagers, but also had a positive demonstration effect on the future use of clean energy in Sudan._x000D_ _x000D_ The value of the equipment is unknown._x000D_ _x000D_

leads.title: International Poverty Reduction Center in China finances phase I of the Joint Program of Scaling up the Maize Labor Intensification System in Morogoro (Linked to #68532, #85130)
leads.place: This project directly benefited more than 200 rural households in Peapea village in Ludewa and Kilosa Districts in the Morogoro Region. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/5842446313.
leads.description: In 2011, China Agriculture University (CAU) began working with Tanzanian authorities and Sokoine University of Agriculture to launch the Joint Program of Scaling up the Maize Labor Intensification System in Morogoro (or Double One Project). This program was implemented in two different phases. This project captures the first phase also called Labor-intensive and Low-investment Maize Production Technology Demonstration Project in Peapea Village. It was financed by the International Poverty Reduction Center in China (IPRCC).   The purpose of this project was to increase crop yields and increase farmers' incomes in Tanzania. Starting in 2014, experts from CAU along with new farming technology travelled to Tanzania to test-run new maize cultivations in 12 experimental households. Due to this initial success, the Chinese government carried out this project in two phases across several more villages. Phase II of this project is recorded in #85130. In 2018, CAU launched a new project (#68532) intended to expand and improve upon the two previous phases.   According to a press release from the China Institute for South-South Cooperation in Agriculture (CISSCA) (p. 4), the first phase of tec
leads.staff_comments: The International Poverty Reduction Center in China is started by the State Council of China, China Ministry of Commerce and UNDP. Hence, these 3 organizations have been coded as the funding agencies.

leads.title: China finances phase II of the Joint Program of Scaling up the Maize Labor Intensification System in Morogoro (Linked to #68532, #68530)
leads.place: The Tanzania-China Joint Research Center for Agricultural Development was set up at the Sokoine University of Agriculture (SUA). Furthermore, Mtego wa Simba was selected as the demonstration village, and four surrounding villages as the extension villages. More detailed locational information can be found at:Sokoine University of Agriculture: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1010487566 Morogoro: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/1600804

leads.title: Chinese Government donates sugar, rice, cooking oil, and medicines for humanitarian relief
leads.description: The Chinese Government provided a humanitarian aid package — including sugar, rice, cooking oil, and medicines — to Yemen in September 2011. The aid was intended to address the humanitarian crisis caused by armed conflict and resettlement of refugees in Yemen. These goods started to be given out to Yemenis in Oman in March 2012.
leads.staff_comments: The monetary value of this aid package is unknown.

leads.title: MOFCOM provides grant for China-Indonesia Hybrid Rice Technical Cooperation Project (Linked to Project ID#71470)
leads.place: The project sought to develop hybrid rice technology in order to increase rice yields in Indonesia. It initially sought to establish a demonstration site (experimental field) in Negara Ratu Village, Natar District, South Lampung Regency. It eventually sought to establish more than 10 demonstration sites in 7 major rice-growing provinces across Indonesia. For more detailed location information: https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/1308291772
leads.description: In December 2008, the Chinese Government and Government of Indonesia signed an exchange of letters regarding the China-Indonesia Hybrid Rice Technical Cooperation Project. China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) provided grant funding for this project, but the monetary value of the grant is unknown.   The project sought to develop hybrid rice technology in order to increase rice yields in Indonesia. It initially sought to establish a demonstration site (experimental field) in Negara Ratu Village, Natar District, South Lampung Regency. It eventually sought to establish more than 10 demonstration sites in 7 major rice-growing provinces across Indonesia. China Yuan Longping High-Tech Agriculture Co., Ltd. and the Indonesian National Academy of Agriculture were jointly responsible for project implementation.    The implementation phase began on May 1, 2010, covering joint scientific research, popularization and technical training in hybrid rice cultivation, and the localization of hybrid rice seed, sharing rice hybrid cultivation technology. On December 29, 2010, the Indonesian Ministry of Agriculture held a project commencement ceremony. Implementation was expected to take place from 20
leads.staff_comments: The Chinese project title is 印尼杂交水稻技术合作项目. The Indonesian project title is kerjasama teknik padi hibrida Indonesia-China. This project is also known as the China High-Yielding Hybrid Rice Demonstration Project.

leads.title: China conducts Phase II of Juncao Project in Lesotho (Linked to #21745, #55681, #55682)
leads.description: According the the Chinese National Engineering Research Center for Juncao Technology, a team of experts from Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University (FAFU) sponsored by the Chinese Ministry of Commerce conducted phase II of the Juncao Technical Demonstration Cooperation Project (援莱索托菌草技术合作项目第二期) in Lesotho between January 2010 and January 2012. China also carried out phase I (#21745), phase III (#55681) and phase IV (#55682)._x000D_ _x000D_ "Jun" (菌) means fungus and "cao" (草) means grass. Juncao, invented in 1986 by a Chinese scientist, refers to the practice of using herb plants to cultivate edible fungi. Since the project's initial signing in October 2006, Chinese experts from FAFU have been developing the Zhonglai Juncao Technology Demonstration Base in Maseru and training local Basotho the agricultural techniques to grow and the entrepreneurial skills to sell. _x000D_ _x000D_ Lesotho's agricultural industry cannot adequately feed the population yet small-scale farming is common. Instead of heavily relying in food imports, Juncao could be a cheap, nutritious alternative for Basotho to feed their families and communities._x000D_ _x000D_ It is unclear if the initial inter-gove

At the time of signing, phase 6 (#63901) was completed. leads.title: Xinhua News offers workshop for Zimbabwean photojournalists
leads.description: In 2010, more than 30 Zimbabwean photojournalists were expected to attend a workshop organized by Xinhua News Agency, the Chinese Embassy, and the Ministry of Media, Information, and Publicity. Xinhua Senior Photographer Ding Mei was to lead the training course. The journalists will be capturing images of project being completed under the Forum for China-Africa Cooperation, like the China agricultural Technology Demonstration Center at Gwebi Agricultural College and the Mahusekwa Hospital in Marondera. Information Minister Webster Shamu was to open the workshop. It is unclear exactly what the dates of the workshop are.

leads.title: Chinese Government provides grant for Phase 2 of Agricultural Project (Linked to #56130)
leads.place: Chinese Government provides a grant for Phase 1 of the Agricultural Project which involved the repair of farmland water conservancy facilities in Bongor and establishing a 30-hectare agricultural technology demonstration center in Koundoul, a suburb of N'Djamena. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/252509153 and https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/2389208990.
leads.description: On March 17, 2009, the Chinese Government and the Government of Chad signed letters of exchange related to Phase 2 of the Agricultural Project. China’s Ministry of Commerce is the source of grant funding for this project. The monetary value of this grant commitment is unknown.   The project involved the provision of technical guidance; the repair of farmland water conservancy facilities in a 3,000-hectare rice area in the town of Bongor, and the establishment of 30-hectare agricultural technology demonstration center in Koundoul, a suburb of N'Djamena (援乍得农业技术示范基地). The agricultural technology demonstration center was designed to include offices, training facilities, rice and crop production demonstration fields, pumping stations, and irrigation facilities. Upon completion, it was envisaged that the center would perform a variety of functions, such as demonstration planting, cultivation, agricultural product processing, and technical training.   On October 6, 2009, a groundbreaking ceremony took place. Chinese Ambassador Yang Guangyu, Political Counselor Chen Guangguo, Business Counselor Huang Mingyuan, and Chadian Minister of Agriculture Naimbaye Losimian, attended the ceremony. H
leads.staff_comments: The French project title is Centre de démonstration technique agricole. The Chinese project title is 二期农业项目.This project is also known as Phase 2 of the Agricultural Technical Cooperation Project.

leads.title: Chinese Government dispatches agricultural experts to Ghana
leads.description: In 2007, the Chinese Government pledged to send senior agricultural experts and youth volunteers to Ghana to render various services. In September 2009, 3 agricultural experts specializing in irrigation, rice and fishery arrived in Ghana. The specialists guided the construction planning of agricultural and fishery demonstration bases for Chinese-funded enterprises and provided fish pond design and scientific and technological consultation for 10 local farms. They returned to China on September 1, 2010. The monetary value of this technical assistance mission is unknown.

leads.title: Chinese agricultural experts assisted Guinea-Bissau with building 11 Rice Growing Demonstration Areas
leads.description: In 2009, Chinese agricultural experts helped build 11 demonstration areas for paddy rice, with a total growing area of 2,000 ha. They bred 530 tonnes of fine strains of rice, which were planted in areas totaling 3,530 ha. Several of the rice strains produced an output three times or more than the original output.
leads.staff_comments: The only source for this record is the Chinese white paper on foreign aid, which reported on aid up to 2009. This could mean the figures above are aggregates of all Chinese agricultural research operations in Guinea-Bissau, not a specific project. Possibly related to ID#16.

leads.title: Chinese Embassy donates office and educational equipment to the Iraqi Ministry of Foreign Affairs
leads.place: This donation went to the Iraqi Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the capital city of Iraq, Baghdad. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/4102222590.
leads.description: On October 22, 2009, the Chinese Embassy in Iraq donated office and educational equipment, such as computers, printers, and projectors, to the Foreign Service Institute, an institution affiliated with the Iraqi Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in the capital city of Baghdad. The donation from the embassy was intended to aid the development of Iraqi education in foreign affairs. The donation to support the ministry came after a truck bombing terrorist attack on the Iraqi Ministry of Foreign Affairs on August 19, 2009 killed or wounded hundreds of faculty, staff, and students of the institute and ministry. The monetary value of this donation is unknown.

leads.title: [China-Venezuela Joint Fund] CDB funds USD 25 million Jose Ignacio de Abreu e Lima Socialist Agriculture Project (linked to project ID#58677, 37528)
leads.place: Anzoátegui StateSee 'DESARRQLLO Y TRANSFERENCIA TECNOLOGICA DEL CULTIVO DE SOYA' for location information.
leads.description: On October 9, 2009, the Jose Ignacio de Abreu e Lima Socialist Agriculture Project (Spanish: Producción Agraria José Ignacio Abreu e Lima, Integral Socialista José Ignacio Abreu e Lima), a collaboration between the governments of Venezuela and Brazil, was announced by Luis Inácio Lula Da Silva of Brazil and Hugo Chavez of Venenzuela. It is named after a Brazilian soldier who fought for Venezuelan independence, and involved the planned cultivation of 35,000 hectares of soybeans, the construction of a flavored drinks plant, an animal feed processing plant, a soybean oil processing plant, a flour mill, 491 homes, recreation areas, squares, a supermarket, a school, a medical assistance center and a radio service. The total project cost exceeded USD 600 million, but most of the funding came from the governments of Venezuela and Brazil. USD 25 million for the project came from the China-Venezuela Joint Fund (see project ID#58677) Tranche B (see project ID#37528).   The project was extended in 2014 with a completion date of December 31, 2017, although none of the production plants exceeded 1% progress. Consumable foods (texturized protein and flavored drinks plants) only advanced 0.69%; t
leads.staff_comments: 1. No transaction amount is included for this project because it is captured by the China-Venezuela Joint Fund (project ID#37528).

leads.title: Chinese Government dispatches 10 agricultural experts to Agricultural Technology Demonstration Center at Gwebi Agricultural College (linked to #20216)
leads.place: This project involved the establishment of an Agricultural Technological Demonstration Center (ATDC) at Gwebi Agricultural College, which is located 27 km outside Harare. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.google.com/maps/place/Gwebi+College+of+Agriculture/@-17.4851029,29.7188816,12z/data=!4m5!3m4!1s0x1937155555555555:0xec50080e46f53b92!8m2!3d-17.4851029!4d29.7889248 and https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/498242336
leads.description: In June 2009, the Chinese Government agreed to send 10 senior Chinese agricultural experts to Zimbabwe to provide technical assistance related to grain production, animal disease prevention and control, dryland farming, and irrigation.  The ten senior Chinese agricultural experts arrived in Zimbabwe on October 25, and were to serve from October 2009 to October 2010 and provide assistance at the Chinese Government-financed Agricultural Technological Demonstration Center (ATDC) of Gwebi Agricultural College. The funding for the ATDC is captured in the linked project #20216. This project is thought to be completed.

leads.title: Chinese Agricultural Flower Assistance to Grenada in 2008 (linked to #54764)
leads.place: No location info available.
leads.description: In November 2008 a team of experts from Chinese Academy of Tropical Agricultural Sciences visited Grenada to assist in a agriculture exchange based around flowers.The visit lasted from November 19 to December 3, 2008. The team inspected progress of the flower-growing program, gave demonstrations, and provided planting guidance. It also organized a presentation titled "International and Chinese Flower Industry Development Overview" for officials of the Grenadian Ministry of Agriculture and others. This exchange is considered under Phase 2 of the Granada Agricultural Technical Cooperation Agreement which includes actively implementing the agricultural procedures.
leads.staff_comments: This project is linked to umbrella project #54764. It ties into the wider Grenada Agricultural Technical Cooperation Project effort established from 2005 which aims to share agricultural technology and knowledge between China and Grenada.

leads.title: China sends team of agricultural specialists
leads.description: On December 24, 2008, a team of advanced Chinese agricultural specialists arrived in Mali to complete a one-year mission. During the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation in November 2006, several new measures for agricultural cooperation in Africa were discussed, including the construction of agricultural demonstration centers and the dispatch of 50 agricultural technology teams to train 2,000 agricultural technicians for African countries._x000D_ _x000D_ The team sent to Mali cooperated with the Mali Agricultural Research Department to conduct small-scale experimental planting of hybrid maize and rice in the Bagineda Irrigation District near Bamako. On December 16, 2009, a delegation of agricultural experts from China visited Mali to review the work completed by the team of specialists and discuss further agricultural cooperation.

leads.title: China sponsored a journalist tour of several cities throughout China for journalists from Samoa
leads.description: In 2008 China sponsored a journalist tour of several cities throughout China for journalists from Samoa.  They were also present for the meeting of Samoan and Chinese dignitaries, and the trade expo. _x000D_ _x000D_ The New York Times reports that a Media Tour in April 2008 was disrupted by Tibetan Monks waving the Tibetan flag. It is also possible the Media Tour was related to the 2008 Olympics, hosted in Beijing. It is unclear if this tour of Samoan journalists was one of the tours disrupted by the Tibetan demonstrations.

leads.title: China signs complementary agreement (Phase II) with Sierra Leone for Rice Growing Demonstration Project (linked to #62528
leads.place: The purpose of the project is for the Rice Growing Demonstration Project. More detailed location information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/27565056
leads.description: On January 22, 2008, the Chinese embassy in Sierra Leone signed a complementary agreement (Phase II) with the Sierra Leonean government, represented by its Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, to implement the Rice Growing Demonstration Project. The project will be carried out by the Department of Agriculture of Hubei Province which will provide technologies to grow hybrid rice that was first cultivated in China. According to a report from the Food and Agricultural Organization of the UN, the introduction of a Chinese hybrid rice variety, along with the use of animal waste as fertilizer improved rice yield from 0.9 to 4.1 tonnes/ha as part of the Chinese government's cooperation with the FAO in the South-South Cooperation project.   This is the second phase of the agreement signed in 2006 (#62528).

leads.title: PetroChina donates two demonstration farms and provides agricultural training in South Kordofan
leads.place: The purpose of the project is to donate two demonstration farms and provide agricultural training in South Kordofan. More detailed location information can be found at: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/3774663
leads.description: In 2008, PetroChina (a subsidary of China National Petroleum Corporation) donated two demonstration farms in Block 6, a part of the South Kordofan region where they have engaged in oil exploration (中石油援建南科尔多凡州的两处示范农场). The company also specially hired agronomists with many years of practical experience from China to train local people for free, teach them to grow food, vegetables and flowers, increase their hematopoietic function, master the ability of self-reliance, and improve living standards through agricultural cultivation.
leads.staff_comments: The total value of the farms and training was reported to be tens of thousands of dollars, but the exact number is unknown. The exact start and end dates of this project are also unknown.

leads.title: China Development Bank disburses unknown amount to China Sonangol International Holding Ltd. to acquire 49% stake in Air Tanzania and purchase planes (Linked to #59666)
leads.place: One purchased plane crashed in April 2012 at Kigoma Airport in western Tanzania. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/178748240.
leads.description: In 2008, the China Development Bank (CDB) signed an agreement committing to loan $21 million USD to China Sonangol International Holding Ltd. for acquiring 49% ownership stake in Air Tanzania Corporation Ltd. (ATCL), a state-owned airline. The proceeds of the loan were reportedly also to be used to buy a number of planes for Air Tanzania. Project #59666 captures the initial loan commitment of $21 million USD. Because it was subsequently cancelled, this project captures the unspecified disbursed amount.   According to a report from the African Center for Strategic Studies (p. 45-46), "by July 2010, it seemed that the China Sonangol-Air Tanzania partnership had been abandoned, as Tanzanian newspapers reported that the country’s national airline would instead forge a partnership with Air Zimbabwe." According to media reports, it seems as if some of the loan was spent on at least three aircrafts. One was a Dash 8 300 series operated by Air Tanzania crashed in April 2012 at Kigoma Airport in western Tanzania, injuring 35 passengers and four crew members. The aircraft is now a write-off.

In August 2009, China CAMC Engineering pledged to carry out the third phase of the irrigation project in the Calabozo district of the state of Guarico, which is valued at 150 million USD and is expected to operate at full capacity in 2012. leads.title: China donates rice to Guinea-Bassau
leads.description: China donated 2,000 tons of rice to Guinea-Bassau, which allowed the regime to address the most basic immediate needs of the population while buying vital time for further shipments to arrive. This Chinese gesture may have prevented serious civil unrest, and it certainly enhanced China’s image in the eyes of the government and people. In August 2007, this first rice shipment was followed by an even larger one of 30,000 tons.

leads.title: Chinese Government provides grant for Phase 1 of Agricultural Project (Linked to #56133)
leads.place: Chinese Government provides a grant for Phase 1 of the Agricultural Project which involved the repair of farmland water conservancy facilities in Bongor and establishing a 30-hectare agricultural technology demonstration center in Koundoul, a suburb of N'Djamena. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/252509153 and https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/2389208990.
leads.description: In 2006, China’s Ministry of Commerce provided a grant to the Government of Chad for Phase 1 of the Agricultural Project. The monetary value of this grant commitment is unknown. The project involved the provision of technical guidance; the repair of farmland water conservancy facilities in a 3,000-hectare rice area in Bongor, and the establishment of 30-hectare agricultural technology demonstration center in Koundoul, a suburb of N'Djamena.   Zhejiang Academy of Agricultural Sciences (由浙江农科院) and China Agricultural Economic and Technical Cooperation Group (中国农业经济技术合作组) were the contractors responsible for implementation. China Agricultural Economic and Technical Cooperation Group dispatched a team of 6 technical experts from Zhejiang Academy of Agricultural Sciences and a second team on May 22, 2007. Phase 1 was completed but its precise implementation end date is unknown. The Chinese Government provided a grant for Phase 2 of the Agricultural Project in 2009 (See #56133).
leads.staff_comments: The Chinese project title is 农业项目. This project is also known as Phase 1 of the Agricultural Technical Cooperation Project.

leads.title: China sent 14 agricultural experts to Chad in 2006
leads.description: On April 27, 2007, Wang Yingwu and State Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Relations Altman signed an exchange of letters on agricultural technology cooperation on behalf of their respective governments. The Chinese side agreed to send 14 agricultural technicians to help Cha implement irrigation and water conservancy in the 3,000 hectares of Bangor rice fields. Facility maintenance and agricultural technology promotion, restoration of 40 hectares of rice and vegetable demonstration bases in Kundule County, outskirts of N’Djamena, and provision of technical guidance for 24 hectares of rice and vegetable demonstration bases in the Jidiya Reclamation Area in the suburbs of N’Djamena from time to time, and On-site training of technicians from agricultural research institutions._x000D_ _x000D_ On December 13, 2006, China sent a team of 6 from the China Aid Agricultural Technology Group to Chad, and the second batch of 8 experts arrived on May 22, 2007 (中国援乍农技组). The agricultural technology group was dispatched by the Zhejiang Academy of Agricultural Sciences. Currently, nine experts are resident in the village of Kolobo, Bangor City. Five experts are resident in N’Djamena.
leads.staff_comments: The first batch of experts arrived in Chad in 2006, so the commitment year is recorded as 2006.

leads.title: Chinese Government funds feasibility study for China-Africa Desertification Control Demonstration and Training Center Project (Linked to Project ID#60679, ID#60680, and ID#72451)
leads.description: In August 2006, the Egyptian Desert Research Center and the Science and Technology Center of Ningxia Autonomous Region signed a Science and Technology Cooperation Agreement  (中国宁夏回族自治区科学技术厅、埃及国家沙漠研究中心科技合作协议). The agreement was signed during a visit to Ningxia, China, by Dr. Ismail Abdel Galil Hussein, Chairman of the Desert Research Center of Egypt, and Prof. Mohamed Abbas Mabrouk, Vice Chairman. The agreement was designed to facilitate Chinese-Egyptian cooperation on the development of bio-fertilizer production technology and efforts to control desertification. It called for an exchange of experts, plans, and information, as well as the joint management and planning of desertification control  programs and demonstration areas.    Then, on March 9, 2014, the Chinese Ambassador to Egypt, Song Aiguo, and Egyptian Minister of Investment and International Cooperation, Dr. Ashraf Al Araby, signed an exchange of letters regarding a feasibility study for the establishment of a China-Africa Desertification Control Demonstration and Training Center Project in Egypt (援埃中非荒漠化防治示范和培训中心项目可行性考察任务政府换文). Since the signature of the agreement, Egypt has sent students and experts to the Ningxia Auton
leads.staff_comments: The Chinese project title is 埃中非荒漠化防治示范和培训中心项目.

leads.title: Chinese Government provides grant for Malaria Prophylactic Therapeutic Demonstration Centre Project (linked to #1741 and #1750)

leads.description: On June 18, 2006, the Chinese Government and the Government of Ghana signed a grant agreement for the establishment of a center that could perform anti-malarial treatments at the Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital in Accra. The monetary value of this grant commitment is unknown. This project was officially completed and handed over to the Ghanaian authorities on October 27, 2009 at a ceremony that held at the Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital. The Chinese Government also donated a batch of anti-malarial drugs worth RMB 2 million to the center (captured in Project ID #1750).   This project is linked to project #1741, which captures a $66 million low-interest loan to fund a telecommunications upgrade and other projects in the country, including expansion and upgrading of the telecommunication network (#43357), and the construction of a primary school, and a malaria center (this project).

The monetary value of this donation is unknown. Yunnan Machinery & Equipment Import & Export (YMEC or 雲南機械進出口股份有限公司) was the contractor responsible for implementation. The project was completed on June 14, 2007 when the handover of the Chinese donation materials was held in Bissau. leads.title: China pledges to construct 250mW coal power plant in Senegal
leads.place: Dakar
leads.description: In April of 2006, the Chinese government pledged to build a 250 MW coal-fired power plant near the capital city of Dakar in Senegal, with financing provided by the Chinese government. The implementing company is China Metallurgical Group Corporation (MCC). Work is to be completed in three years, and the plant is to consist of two turbines generating 125 MW a piece.This project may be tied because MCC was offered iron mining rights by state-owned Societe des Mines de Fer du Senegal Oriental (Miferso) following this project. The current status of this project cannot be found, but the most recent report said the bid has yet to be published due to rising concern over the pollution a coal-fired plant would create. According to sources, China was due to complete construction in 2011, however, no evidence of completion has been found. A Korean company has also funded a 250MW plant, which could indicate that China is no longer funding such a project.

leads.title: Chinese Government dispatches experts for the Senegal Agricultural Technical Assistance Project between 2006 and 2020 (Linked to #41896)
leads.place: The Chinese Government began sending agricultural technical assistance teams to demonstration centers in Podor and Sangalkam. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/12982168 and https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/12989624.
leads.description: In November 2006, the Chinese Government began sending agricultural technical assistance teams to demonstration centers in Podor and Sangalkam. This project was financed by the China Ministry of Commerce and implemented by the Senegal Ministry of Agriculture.   In Sangalkam, the agricultural technical training teams teach local farmers how to grow vegetable produce. In Podor, the teams taught local farmers new ways to grow rice. Between 2007 and 2009, these teams trained 420 farmers.  Over the same period, rice crop growth per hectare tripled — from 3 tonnes of rice to 9 tonnes of rice per hectare. By 2015, six different agricultural technical cooperation missions had served in Podor and Sangalkam. The most recent phase was supposed to serve in Senegal until mid-2020.   On March 24, 2015, the Chinese Government signed an exchange of letters committing an additional CFA 877 million in grant funding for subsequent phases of the Senegal Agricultural Technical Assistance Project (see Project #41896).
leads.staff_comments: Chinese names: 中援塞农业技术队 or 中国塞内加尔农业组It is unclear how/whether the Covid-19 pandemic interrupted this project.

leads.title: The People's Liberation Army airlifts survival kits to countries hit by the Indian Ocean tsunami
leads.place: All tsunami hit countries
leads.description: China's government has donated more than $60 million, sent four medical teams, and airlifted survival kits to countries hit by the Indian Ocean tsunami in January 2006. The People's Liberation Army has airlifted nearly 500 tons of food, water, supplies, and medical and telecom equipment to affected areas, the WHO said. In addition, with the large donation provided by the Chinese government, the Health Ministry has sent 164 medical personnel to Thailand and Sri Lanka to help save lives and prevent the spread of diseases that the WHO fears could dramatically raise the death count beyond the approximately 150,000 tsunami victims confirmed dead so far.

leads.title: Chinese medical team sent over to help Indonesian tsunami survivors
leads.place: On January 25, 2005, a 20-person Chinese medical team arrived in Banda Aceh for a relief mission. For more detailed location information: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/5978331
leads.description: On January 25, 2005, a 20-person Chinese medical team arrived in Banda Aceh for a relief mission. The team, also known as the fourth international medical team for Indian Ocean Tsunami relief, comprised 20 medical personnel from different hospitals and health organizations in Beijing and Tianjin. In the following 11 days, the doctors treated more than 1,200 people at the General Hospital of Banda Aceh, one-third of patients at the hospital. During their work in Banda Aceh, the Chinese medical team inspected camps of displaced people around the city and conducted emergency hygienic assessments of the camps in cooperation with the United Nations Children's Fund. The team returned to China on February 6.
leads.staff_comments: The four international medical teams for Indian Ocean Tsunami relief are #34816 (2 teams to Thailand), #33231 (1 team to Sri Lanka), and #35113 (1 team to Indonesia). China contributed 63 million USD for tsunami relief in total, most of the individual project are captured (see projects linked with resource #41811).

leads.title: Chinese Government grants pollution and environmental equipment to Russia following a chemical plant explosion in Jilin City
leads.place: The Chinese Government granted equipment to Russia following an explosion of the No.102 Petrochemical Plant in Jilin City, Jilin Province, China, which led to pollution in the Songhua and Amur rivers. More detailed locational information can be found at:Jilin City: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/2764055Songhua River: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/2237734Amur River: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/367888945
leads.description: On 3 December 2005 the Chinese Government granted pollution and environmental equipment to Russia following an explosion of an industrial plant owned by Jilin Petrochemical Company, part of CNPC, which led to pollution in the Songhua and Amur rivers. China offered six sets of liquid chromatograph equipment and 150 tons of active carbon. Later on December 16th, China provided a second batch of water testing and purifying materials, including 1,000 more tons of active carbon.  One available source claims that the media around 20 December 2005 reported that nearly 3000 Chinese nationals aided in the construction of a dam to protect the water supply in the city of Khabarovsk.  It is unclear if CNPC or some other Chinese Government Institution is providing the aid.

leads.title: Chinese Government provides an interest-free loan for the Kébir River Dam Construction Project
leads.place: The purpose of this project was to construct a dam on the Kébir River near the town of Tabarka (Dabarka) within the Gafsa Governorate. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/128504309.
leads.description: On March 9, 2004 and March 10, 2004, the Chinese Government and the Government of Tunisia signed an exchange of letters, which committed an interest-free loan for the Kébir River Dam Construction Project. Then, on April 8, 2004, the Tunisian Parliament passed a law, approving the interest-free loan. In addition to the Chinese Government, the Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development provided a $28 million loan for this project in 2000. The primary purpose of this project was to construct a dam on the Kébir River near the town of Tabarka (Dabarka) within the Gafsa Governorate  (ولاية قفصة‎) to address irrigation and residential water shortages in the region. It consisted of 3 components: the construction of a clay core rockfill dam (with water storage capacity of 64 million cubic meters), the construction of a spillway tunnel, and the construction of a water pipeline. The dam was designed to be 70 meters high and 10 meters wide. Its crest was designed to be 560 meters long. Upon completion, the dam was designed to transport 35 million cubic meters of water per year to the Sidi Barrak Reservoir and reduce the risk of flooding within the Gafsa Governorate. leads.title: Chinese Government dispatches experts to advise on reconstruction planning after 2003 Boumerdès earthquake (Linked to Project ID#14)
leads.place: This project was designed to support earthquake response and reconstruction activities in Boumerdès Province. More detailed locational information can be found at https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/1283608#map=11/36.7361/3.6312
leads.description: In July 2003, the Chinese Government dispatched a team of reconstruction planning experts to Algeria to analyze the damage caused by the 2003 Boumerdès earthquake.   On July 6, 2003, the expert team arrived in Algiers. Under the arrangement of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning of Algeria, experts conducted a field visit to the epicenter. The team was to advise the Government of Algeria on the best course of action to ensure a speedy recovery. On July 26, 2003, the team returned to China.
leads.staff_comments: The 2003 Boumerdès earthquake occurred on May 21, 2003 at 19:44:21 local time in northern Algeria. The shock had a moment magnitude of 6.8 and a maximum Mercalli intensity of X (Extreme). The epicentre of the earthquake was located near the town of Thénia in Boumerdès Province, approximately 60 km east of the capital Algiers. The quake was the strongest to hit Algeria in more than twenty years – since 1980, when a magnitude 7.1 earthquake resulted in at least 2,633 deaths. Approximately 2,266 people were killed, 10,261 injured, and 200,000 left homeless as a result of the earthquake. Reports indicate more than 1,243 buildings were completely or partially destroyed. Infrastructure was predictably damaged in Algiers, Boumerdès, Réghaïa and Thénia; roads in Algeria are generally of high quality, but many city streets and local roads were difficult to traverse because of debris from collapsed buildings. Overall, the Boumerdès Province was the hardest-hit region. In the Boumerdès Province, several cities were heavily damaged, with Thénia, Zemmouri, and Boumerdès, being the worst affected.

leads.title: Chinese government provided support and granted the Small-Scale Agricultural Demonstration Farm Project
leads.description: On November 14, 2003, Wang Longqing, president of the Tianjin Academy of Agricultural Sciences, and Tuita, Minister of Agriculture of the Tonga, signed specific implementation measures to assist Tonga in establishing a small demonstration farm. According to the agreement, China would help establish the farm, send four agricultural experts to work in Tonga for one year, plant new varieties of vegetables and fruits, test a small number of poultry, train local agricultural technicians, and provide farm equipment and supplies.   The vegetable garden was opened on April 6, 2004. On November 10, 2004, the transfer ceremony of the aid small demonstration farm was held on site. Ambassador Gao Shanhai and Minister of Agriculture of Tutu signed a transfer certificate on behalf of the governments of the two countries, marking the successful conclusion of the technical cooperation project of the first China-Tonga demonstration farm.

leads.description: On July 21, 2002, Nauru's Acting President Remy Namaduk and the Chinese Assistant Foreign Minister Zhou Wenzhong signed a joint communiqué, establishing diplomatic relations between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Republic of Nauru. The Chinese Government also reportedly agreed to provide $60 million of grant assistance (captured via Project ID#37645) and help the Government of Nauru resolve a $77 million outstanding debt to General Electric Capital Corporation in exchange for the Government of the Republic of Nauru cutting ties with Taiwan and recognizing Beijing's One China Policy. leads.staff_comments: On July 21, 2002, then President René Harris of Nauru signed a joint communiqué in Hong Kong to establish diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China (PRC).  In the document, the Government of the Republic of Nauru recognized that 'there is but one China in the world, that the Government of the People's Republic of China is the sole legal government representing the whole of China and that Taiwan is an inalienable part of Chinese territory.' The declaration also contained an undertaking by Nauru to close its embassy in Taipei within one month, despite the fact Nauru had never had a diplomatic mission in Taiwan. This move followed the PRC's promise to provide a large aid package. That same day, the Republic of China (ROC or Taiwanese) government issued an ultimatum, demanding that the communiqué be withdrawn within 24 hours or it would take the initiative and sever diplomatic ties. There was much dissension within the Nauruan government over the move by Harris, which the President was alleged to have made on his own initiative. fields.likely_already_on_map: three or more distinctive words shared with a case in the same country. Confirm before dropping the row.
fields.possible_overlap: only two shared words, which in this dataset is mostly noise. Treat as open.
fields.matching: likely_already_on_map and possible_overlap are keyword hints, not findings. They match rare words shared with a case in the same country, so two projects in the same state can match each other. Confirm a row before dropping it; nothing has been deleted from these lists.
